'''Thomas N. Seyfried''' (born 1946<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dlib.bc.edu/islandora/object/bc-ir:102683|title=Interview with Thomas N. Seyfried on Cancer as a metabolic disease: On the origin, management, and prevention of cancer|access-date=2023-03-12}}</ref>) is an American professor of biology, genetics, and biochemistry at [[Boston College]].

==Education and early life==
His father, William E. Seyfried, Sr., served in the [[United States Merchant Marine]] during World War II and was president and founder of Capeway Paints in [[Brockton, Massachusetts]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.currentobituary.com/obit/56756|title=Obituary: William E. Seyfried, Sr., 85 |access-date=2023-03-12}}</ref>  His brother William E. Seyfried, Jr. is a [[University of Minnesota]] professor in the Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cse.umn.edu/esci/william-seyfried8|title=University of Minnesota: William Seyfried|access-date=2023-03-12}}</ref> Seyfried served in the United States Army during the [[Vietnam War]], receiving the [[Bronze Star Medal|Bronze Star]], the [[Air Medal]], and the [[Commendation Medal|Army Commendation Medal]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Thomas N. Seyfried bio at Amazon.com|isbn=978-0470584927 |last1=Seyfried |first1=Thomas |date=26 June 2012 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons }}</ref>

Seyfried received his PhD in genetics and neurochemistry from the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]] in 1976.  His postdoctoral fellowship studies were in the Department of Neurology at the [[Yale School of Medicine|Yale University School of Medicine]] where he served as an assistant professor in neurology.  He did undergraduate work at St. Francis College in Brooklyn, NY (United States), and received a master's degree in genetics from [[Illinois State University|Illinois State University, Normal]].

== Career and Research ==

Seyfried's research focuses on mechanisms of chronic diseases such as cancer, epilepsy, neurodegenerative lipid storage diseases, and caloric restriction diets.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bc.edu/bc-web/schools/mcas/departments/biology/people/faculty-directory/thomas-seyfried.html|title=Biology Department Faculty: Thomas N. Seyfried, professor|access-date=2023-03-12}}</ref>  He is known for his 2012 book ''Cancer as a Metabolic Disease: On the Origin, Management, and Prevention of Cancer''. Some of his papers, "Cancer as a metabolic disease" (2010) and "On the origin of cancer metastasis" (2013) have been extensively cited in the academic literature.<ref>Seyfried, T. N.; Shelton, L. M. (2010). "Cancer as a metabolic disease: implications for long-term survival". ''Nutrition & Metabolism''. '''7''': 7.</ref><ref>Seyfried, T. N.; Huysentruyt, L. C. (2013). "On the origin of cancer metastasis". ''Critical Reviews in Oncogenesis''. '''18''' (1–2): 43–73.</ref><ref>Thomas N. Seyfried, Google Scholar profile, https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=ctSRQrsAAAAJ&hl=en (accessed 7 October 2026).</ref> 

Seyfried is a popular interview guest where he is a proponent of the [[metabolic theory of cancer]]. Seyfried proposes using the [[ketogenic diet]] in combination with other therapies such as glutamine inhibition in what he calls press/pulse therapy, for the treatment of certain cancers such as glioblastoma.<ref name="Seyfried2017">{{Cite journal |last1=Seyfried |first1=Thomas N. |last2=Yu |first2=George |last3=Maroon |first3=Joseph C. |last4=D’Agostino |first4=Dominic P. |date=2017-02-23 |title=Press-pulse: a novel therapeutic strategy for the metabolic management of cancer |journal=Nutrition & Metabolism |volume=14 |issue=1 |pages=19 |doi=10.1186/s12986-017-0178-2 |doi-access=free |issn=1743-7075 |pmc=5324220 |pmid=28250801}}</ref> While other medical researchers conclude there is insufficient evidence that ketogenic diets are effective treatments for cancer,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Grimes |first1=David Robert |last2=O'Riordan |first2=Elizabeth |date=November 2023 |title=Starving cancer and other dangerous dietary misconceptions |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S1470204523004837 |journal=The Lancet Oncology |language=en |volume=24 |issue=11 |pages=1177–1178 |doi=10.1016/S1470-2045(23)00483-7 |pmid=37922928 |quote=One especially common variant is the ketogenic diet for cancer, pivoting on the assumption that forced physiological ketosis (a normal response to low glucose availability brought on by fasting or low carbohydrate diets) avoids fuelling cancer. This concept has been taken to extremes by some advocates, who assert that ketogenic diets eliminate the need for chemotherapy and radiotherapy. However, there is insufficient evidence to support the efficacy of ketogenic diets in cancer, with only a few, somewhat biased, clinical investigations, with findings that are distinctly at odds with the more sweeping claims made.|url-access=subscription }}</ref> ketogenic diets remain an area of active research; there are ongoing clinical trials evaluating the ketogenic diet in combination with the standard of care.<ref>{{cite web
|title=A Phase 2 Study of the Ketogenic Diet vs Standard Anti-cancer Diet Guidance for Patients With Glioblastoma in Combination With Standard-of-care Treatment |url=https://clinicaltrials.ucsf.edu/trial/NCT05708352 |website=UCSF Clinical Trials |publisher=University of California, San Francisco |access-date=2026-10-07}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Ketogenic Diet and Chemotherapy in Affecting Recurrence in Patients with Stage IV Breast Cancer|url=https://www.cancer.gov/research/participate/clinical-trials-search/v?id=NCI-2017-01168|website=National Cancer Institute|publisher=National Institutes of Health|access-date=2026-10-07}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Klement|first1=Rainer J.|title=Beneficial effects of ketogenic diets for cancer patients: a realist review with focus on evidence and confirmation|journal=Medical Oncology|date=2017-12-13|volume=34|issue=12|pages=216|doi=10.1007/s12032-017-1042-2|pmid=29209515|url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29209515/}}</ref>

Seyfried has expressed criticism of [[radiation therapy]] and [[chemotherapy]], which he has compared to "medieval" treatments.{{cn|date=May 2026}} However, in his peer-reviewed scientific publications, Seyfried has implemented ketogenic metabolic therapy as [[adjuvant therapy]] to standard of care, dose-adjusted chemotherapy and radiation.<ref name="Seyfried2017"/><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Duraj |first1=Tomás |last2=Kalamian |first2=Miriam |last3=Zuccoli |first3=Giulio |last4=Maroon |first4=Joseph C. |last5=D’Agostino |first5=Dominic P. |last6=Scheck |first6=Adrienne C. |last7=Poff |first7=Angela |last8=Winter |first8=Sebastian F. |last9=Hu |first9=Jethro |last10=Klement |first10=Rainer J. |last11=Hickson |first11=Alicia |last12=Lee |first12=Derek C. |last13=Cooper |first13=Isabella |last14=Kofler |first14=Barbara |last15=Schwartz |first15=Kenneth A. |date=2024-12-05 |title=Clinical research framework proposal for ketogenic metabolic therapy in glioblastoma |journal=BMC Medicine |volume=22 |issue=1 |pages=578 |doi=10.1186/s12916-024-03775-4 |doi-access=free |issn=1741-7015 |pmc=11622503 |pmid=39639257}}</ref>

Seyfried is a senior editor for the [[ASN Neuro]] journal, and is on the board of editors for [[Neurochemical Research]], Nutrition & Metabolism, and the [[Journal of Lipid Research]]. He previously served as chair of the Scientific Advisory Committee for the National Tay-Sachs and Allied Diseases Association.
